steps: 1. Record the plan and contract first (specs outrank implementation). Write docs/plans/2026-10-18-resume-projection-integrity.md: the ordering diagram (CLI: schema -> root-checksum precheck -> audit_scope -> observability overrides -> session/process metadata -> WorkflowExecutor -> prologue; executor root: checksum recheck -> audit_scope -> prologue; reached call: visit/start publication -> input/write-root/checksum/bound-input validation -> lineage and callee audit -> child frame creation). Record two assumptions: (a) resume.py currently writes observability overrides before the checksum precheck, so 'nothing written' for item 6 means moving that write after the precheck and the audit; (b) the existing tests/test_resume_command.py and tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py 'projection_resume_*' characterization tests pin today's ordering and get updated to the new contract, not deleted. Add a 'Checksum-compatible resume projection integrity' section to specs/state.md (next to 'State Integrity and Recovery', ~line 235) covering items 1-7 (scope audit and ordering, explicit identities and omission compatibility, loop progress forms, call frames and the Workflow Lisp retry lineage, failure/mutation envelopes, sticky non-routable failure, the diagnostic v1 shape, the twelve reasons, privacy, no receipts/caches/migrations, schema stays 2.1). Add numbered entries after item 199 in specs/acceptance/index.md, one per behaviour group, each naming its proof test module. Files: docs/plans/2026-10-18-resume-projection-integrity.md, specs/state.md, specs/acceptance/index.md.

2. Typed Workflow Lisp provenance (item 8), needed before lineage detection can stop using the .orc suffix. In orchestrator/workflow_lisp/compiler.py (compile_stage3_entrypoint and the helper at ~line 328 that links imported bundles), stamp provenance.frontend_kind='workflow_lisp' with dataclasses.replace on every validated bundle the compiler produces, on imported Workflow Lisp bundles reached through imports, and on every lowered bundle (orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/core.py at the bundle-construction sites ~744/930/1015). Link classic-YAML bundles from imported_workflow_bundles as the same object, unchanged (frontend_kind stays None). In orchestrator/workflow_lisp/build.py:383, build_frontend_bundle keeps the selected bundle's frontend_kind instead of overwriting it (still sets build-root/source-map fields). Change CallExecutor._is_workflow_lisp_target in orchestrator/workflow/calls.py to return provenance.frontend_kind == 'workflow_lisp' only. Tests (TDD, behavioural through compile_stage3_entrypoint / build_frontend_bundle / _is_workflow_lisp_target): a new tests/test_workflow_lisp_frontend_kind_provenance.py covering entry, imported .orc, lowered and classic-YAML-import bundles (identity check with `is`), plus a YAML bundle whose path ends in .orc-looking names still not counted as Workflow Lisp. Files: orchestrator/workflow_lisp/compiler.py, orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/core.py, orchestrator/workflow_lisp/build.py, orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_frontend_kind_provenance.py.

3. Classic-YAML duplicate import aliases (item 5). PyYAML's SafeLoader silently keeps the last duplicate key, so detection has to work on the composed node tree. Add a new module orchestrator/loader_import_aliases.py (loader.py is already 6218 lines) with one function that takes the YAML text, composes it with PreservingLoader (yaml.compose), walks the top-level MappingNode, and collects every effective `imports` section: direct `imports` keys, and `imports` keys inside top-level `<<` merge sources (a single mapping or a sequence of mappings). Inside each section it expands `<<` merges and records each alias key's start_mark as `line L, column C` (1-based). Output: one `imports.<alias>: duplicate import alias` error per alias seen more than once, listing every position; else, if there is more than one section, one `imports: duplicate top-level mapping` error listing each `imports` key's position. A repeated alias is never also reported as a duplicate section. In WorkflowLoader.load (orchestrator/loader.py ~line 177), run it on the file text right after the successful yaml.load and before _load_imports. Report through _add_error and raise WorkflowValidationError so build_loaded_workflow_bundle is never reached. Tests in tests/test_loader_validation.py (or a new tests/test_loader_import_alias_duplicates.py): duplicate keys, a `<<` inside imports, repeated top-level sections (with repeated and with distinct aliases), top-level merge sources carrying imports, merged-plus-explicit, and a single merged section with unique aliases that still loads. Assert exact positions and that bundle construction was not reached (no bundle returned). Files: orchestrator/loader_import_aliases.py, orchestrator/loader.py, tests/test_loader_validation.py.

4. Projection resume slots (public state_projection API). Add the `import_alias: Optional[str] = None` field to CallBoundaryProjection in orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py and populate it from the authored call step's `call` alias in register_call_boundary at orchestrator/workflow/lowering.py:170-186 (thread the alias through its callers in lowering.py). Put the new resume-slot logic in a new module orchestrator/workflow/state_projection_resume.py so state_projection.py stays well under 500 lines: ResumeProjectionValidationError(ValueError) with .reason/.message and str()==message; the frozen dataclasses ResumeSlot (node_id, step_id, presentation_key, region, iteration_index, loop_node_id), ResumeProjectionSlotIndex (candidates_by_step_id, call_boundaries_by_step_id, unclaimed_explicit_rows), ResumeIdentityResolution (slot, candidate_count, exact_identity_candidate_count) and ResumeCallBoundaryResolution (boundary, candidate_count). Also add enumerate_resume_slots(projection, state), which reads state without mutating it. It enumerates top-level body/finalization slots and the loop-local slots for each persisted for_each/repeat_until iteration, using the existing IterationStepKeyProjection.runtime_step_id/step_key, and maps each loop-contained call boundary to its runtime step id per iteration. It validates for_each/repeat_until bookkeeping with exactly the listed reasons and messages: the four repeat_until progress forms; successful exhaustion needs steps.<loop>.status completed with outputs; failed exhaustion needs error.type repeat_until_iterations_exhausted. It also computes unclaimed explicit rows, with the step_id as persisted and copy.deepcopy-snapshotted. Further functions: resolve_resume_step_id(index, step_id, presentation_key=None), where an unhashable or malformed id gives count 0 and an id owned by another presentation key gives slot None and candidate count 1; and resolve_call_boundary(index, call_step_id). Expose the three as thin methods on WorkflowStateProjection with the required signatures. Tests in tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py: every reason/message pair, all four repeat_until forms, loop-local slot iteration_index, finalization region, unhashable ids, no-mutation (deepcopy equality), and the call-boundary resolution count. Files: orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py, orchestrator/workflow/state_projection_resume.py, orchestrator/workflow/lowering.py, tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py.

5. Retry lineage indexing (pure, no I/O). New module orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_lineage.py with RetryFrameMember(frame_id, ordinal), CompletedFrameMember(frame_id), CallFrameRetryLineage(base_frame_id, completed_members, failed_predecessors sorted by ordinal, running_member), CallFrameRetryLineageError(ValueError) with .reason, index_retry_lineage(boundary_step_id, frame_items, *, frontend_kind) and next_unused_retry_frame_id(lineage). Parse ids strictly: `B` is ordinal 0 and `B::retry::<n>` needs a positive decimal n without leading zeros, otherwise unsupported_shape; a nested marker is also unsupported_shape. Map violations to reasons: missing_call_boundary for a call_step_id other than the boundary; persisted_import_alias_mismatch for differing aliases; unknown status -> unsupported_shape; mixed bases, a duplicate ordinal or several running members -> ambiguous_resumable_call_frame. A gap in the failed/running ordinals is unsupported_shape, so ordinals must be contiguous from 0. Non-Workflow-Lisp boundaries allow at most one non-completed frame, which becomes running_member. next_unused_retry_frame_id returns the lowest unused positive ordinal over all members, completed ones included. Tests: new tests/test_call_frame_retry_lineage.py covering each reason, ordering, completed frames of any number, and idempotent allocation. Files: orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_lineage.py, tests/test_call_frame_retry_lineage.py.

6. The scope auditor. New module orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py: ResumeScopePath (frozen; root(), child(), projection_scope, as_context(); __post_init__ snapshots call_frame_ids to a tuple), ResumeProjectionIntegrityError(ValueError) carrying .error, a single _diagnostic(...) builder that always emits all v1 context keys (diagnostic_schema, reason, scope_path, field, offending_value scalar-or-null, expected_owner {workflow_file, workflow_checksum from the audited state, projection_scope}, candidate_count, call_boundary_step_id), and audit_scope(bundle, state, scope_path). The audit runs in this order. Container shapes: steps, call_frames, each frame -> unsupported_shape. enumerate_resume_slots: map ResumeProjectionValidationError.reason to unsupported_shape or invalid_loop_progress, with field taken from the message's dotted prefix. Each steps.<name> row: no step_id is compatible as-is; a present step_id gets resolve_resume_step_id -> unknown_explicit_step_id, presentation_slot_mismatch or unsupported_shape; unclaimed rows -> unclaimed_explicit_step_row. current_step when present: missing_required_identity, out_of_scope_step_id, presentation_slot_mismatch. Each call frame: shape, then call_step_id resolved through resolve_resume_step_id (out_of_scope_step_id) and resolve_call_boundary (missing_call_boundary or ambiguous_call_boundary). Then group frames per boundary with index_retry_lineage, using the frontend_kind of the bundle that the boundary's current import_alias selects through workflow_import_bundle (missing_imported_bundle when it selects none), with lineage errors mapped to reasons. The auditor never recurses by loading anything: nested frames are audited when the call executor reaches them (step 9). It reads only bundle and state: no loader, no checksum, no file I/O, no mutation. Re-export index_retry_lineage, next_unused_retry_frame_id, CallFrameRetryLineage, RetryFrameMember and CallFrameRetryLineageError from call_frame_lineage. Keep the module under 500 lines, moving the diagnostic builder to orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_diagnostics.py if it grows. Avoid the forbidden imports and identifiers: no migration_parity or procedure_identity_retirement, no 'receipt', no audit/projection-integrity 'cache'. Tests in a new tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py through audit_scope on real loaded bundles (WorkflowLoader on tmp YAML fixtures, plus one compiled .orc fixture): one case per reason with its exact field/offending_value/candidate_count; absent-step_id compatibility for completed, skipped, failed, running-loop-frame and result rows; privacy (a malformed list or mapping id and bound inputs never appear in the diagnostic); purity (state deepcopy equal after the call); and a source-level guard that the module text avoids the forbidden imports, names and substrings. Files: orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py, optionally orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_diagnostics.py, tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py.

7. StateManager failure envelopes. In orchestrator/state.py add record_workflow_checksum_mismatch(*, workflow_file, persisted_checksum, current_checksum, reason) and record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(error). Both work on the raw state.json mapping (read it, set only status='failed', error and updated_at, then write atomically with the existing _write_json_atomic) so that unknown root fields, the run tree and current_step stay byte-for-byte unchanged and fail_run is not called. Validate the reason enum and the str|None types up front and fail fast. Tests in tests/test_state_manager.py: JSON diff before/after equals exactly the three-field delta, unknown root keys are preserved, and the envelope shape is exact. Files: orchestrator/state.py, tests/test_state_manager.py.

8. Root ordering: CLI and structural-root executor. In orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py, add a module-level `from orchestrator.workflow.resume_projection_integrity import ResumeScopePath, audit_scope, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError` and call the bare name audit_scope so tests can substitute it. Move the observability merge/_write_state block (~line 390) to after the root-checksum precheck. In the non-force-restart path, run audit_scope(workflow_bundle, state.to_dict(), ResumeScopePath.root(state.workflow_file)) after the checksum precheck and before observability overrides, open_executor_session, write_process_metadata and WorkflowExecutor construction. On failure: state_manager.record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(exc.error), print the message to stderr, return 1. In orchestrator/workflow/executor.py, add a module-level audit_scope import and a _root_resume_guard(state) called in execute() before _execute_prologue when resume is true and the state manager is not a CallFrameStateManager. It recomputes the checksum through self.state_manager.calculate_checksum on the bundle's provenance workflow_path and compares it with the persisted workflow_checksum. Mismatch reasons: missing_recorded_checksum, missing_workflow_path, workflow_unavailable on FileNotFoundError, workflow_modified. On mismatch it calls record_workflow_checksum_mismatch and returns the reloaded failed state; otherwise it calls audit_scope and on failure record_resume_projection_integrity_failure. Either way it returns before the prologue. In resume.py, close the session as 'failed' when result.status is failed; check orchestrator/runtime_observability.py close_executor_session and make it never touch root error/status (and swallow nothing: a close failure is logged after the diagnostic is already persisted). Update the characterization tests in tests/test_resume_command.py (test_projection_resume_integrity_mutation_order_cli_root_explicit_id_corruption, ..._direct_executor_root_..., the schema-boundary test) to the new event order, and add: substitution of resume_command.audit_scope and executor.audit_scope to observe ordering; CLI failure exit 1 with stderr reason and a three-field persisted delta; the initial checksum precheck still writes nothing; executor checksum-recheck envelope for each reason, stopping before the audit; the executor's second audit catching an identity change after the CLI audit passed (substituted audit) with the session closed failed and the diagnostic intact; and a child call-frame executor that does not rerun the root guard. Files: orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py, orchestrator/workflow/executor.py, orchestrator/runtime_observability.py, tests/test_resume_command.py.

9. Reached-call revalidation and lineage execution in orchestrator/workflow/calls.py (with a module-level audit_scope import). In resume mode, replace the first-non-completed-frame scan in frame_id_with_overrides by projection-owned resolution. Call self.executor.projection.resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id) once per reached call identity (positional args), with slot_index from enumerate_resume_slots of the parent state. Exactly one boundary must own it; select the callee with workflow_import_bundle(parent_bundle, boundary.import_alias), not step['call'] (missing_imported_bundle when absent). Check the persisted import_alias, which never redirects. Before any lineage grouping, reject a completed frame whose id equals the frame the call would occupy, whatever its call_step_id, using resume_state_invalid_result(detail='completed_call_frame_id_collision'): the context keys are exactly step/call/call_frame_id/reason/detail, and no child manager or executor is created. Keep the existing order: ordinary visit/start publication, resolve_bound_inputs, finalize_bound_inputs, validate_write_root_bindings, validate_resume_checksum and validate_resume_bound_inputs. Workflow Lisp lineage after index_retry_lineage: a running member's checksum and bound-input checks run first and win (call_resume_checksum_mismatch keeps precedence); then each failed predecessor in ordinal order gets validate_resume_checksum plus audit_scope(callee_bundle, predecessor_state, scope_path.child(id)); then audit_scope on the running member before resuming it. Without a running member, validate and audit every failed predecessor, then allocate next_unused_retry_frame_id(lineage) (this replaces _retry_frame_id/_retry_family_base/_is_failed_retry_family_frame, which get deleted). Non-Workflow-Lisp boundaries audit their single resumable frame. Carry the ResumeScopePath on the executor: a root path from WorkflowExecutor, and a child path passed into the child WorkflowExecutor through a constructor kwarg defaulting to None. Any ResumeProjectionIntegrityError before construction returns {'status':'failed','exit_code':2,'error': exc.error} unchanged, leaving the callee frame untouched. When a child_state error has type resume_projection_integrity_error, return that error unchanged instead of wrapping it in call_failed. Ancestor promotion of the same error to the root happens through the normal failed-step path plus step 10's sticky handling (verify orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_state.py snapshots stay ordinary). Update the projection_resume_* tests in tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py to the new contract and add: callee chosen by current boundary alias when the persisted alias differs (fails persisted_import_alias_mismatch); stale caller id; two resumable frames for one YAML boundary; the completed-frame collision for matching, stale and missing call_step_id; predecessor audit order and the checksum precedence; and nested-scope recursion with the scope_path growing per frame. Update the Workflow Lisp retry expectations in tests/test_workflow_lisp_procedure_first_migrations.py (~1466) to the lowest-unused-ordinal rule. Files: orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, orchestrator/workflow/executor.py (constructor scope-path kwarg), orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_state.py (read-only check, edit only if snapshotting wraps errors), tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_procedure_first_migrations.py.

10. Sticky non-routable projection failure (item 6, last bullet). Add one predicate, is_resume_projection_integrity_error(result_or_error), in orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py, and use it at the shared routing points rather than in every caller. In orchestrator/workflow/executor.py _handle_control_flow, return '_stop' before evaluating success/failure/always routes or on_error=continue. In orchestrator/workflow/loops.py, the for_each and repeat_until iteration drivers stop the loop with that failure (no next iteration, no condition evaluation). Check orchestrator/workflow/transition_executor.py and orchestrator/workflow/outcomes.py for route/outcome consumption and make sure outcome normalisation never reclassifies the error. In orchestrator/workflow/finalization.py, when a cleanup step fails while the run already holds a projection error, record finalization.status='failed' and finalization.failure={'step','step_id','error': the cleanup's projection error or None}, keeping the run error as it is. When the projection error comes only from finalization, it becomes the run error and finalization.failure.error. Make sure _execute_epilogue in executor.py and the session close in resume.py never clear or replace it. Tests in a new tests/test_resume_projection_sticky_failure.py, driven through WorkflowExecutor.execute(resume=True) on YAML fixtures with a corrupted nested call frame: authored success/failure/always routes, on_error continue, for_each and repeat_until continuation, finalization that runs and fails (supplemental record), and a projection error arising only in finalization. Files: orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py, orchestrator/workflow/executor.py, orchestrator/workflow/loops.py, orchestrator/workflow/transition_executor.py, orchestrator/workflow/outcomes.py, orchestrator/workflow/finalization.py, tests/test_resume_projection_sticky_failure.py.

11. Forensic current_step in observability and monitoring. In orchestrator/observability/report.py build_status_snapshot (~286-374): when the run is failed and error.type is resume_projection_integrity_error or workflow_checksum_mismatch, render the unchanged current_step's step as pending (status and summary 'pending', current_visit_count None, counted under pending not running) and skip the stale-heartbeat 'running' inference (~237). render_status_markdown (~458) then never says 'in progress' for it. In orchestrator/monitor/classifier.py (_active_cursor_heartbeat) and orchestrator/monitor/messages.py (_heartbeat_at), do not treat that current_step as live or stalled. Put the forensic-envelope check in one helper (in report.py, imported by monitor) so the error-type set lives in one place. Tests: tests/test_observability_report.py (snapshot counts, step status/summary, markdown) and tests/test_monitor_classifier.py (not stalled, not live). Files: orchestrator/observability/report.py, orchestrator/monitor/classifier.py, orchestrator/monitor/messages.py, tests/test_observability_report.py, tests/test_monitor_classifier.py.

12. Verification and closeout. Run the narrow selectors first: pytest tests/test_call_frame_retry_lineage.py tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py tests/test_state_manager.py tests/test_loader_validation.py tests/test_workflow_lisp_frontend_kind_provenance.py tests/test_resume_projection_sticky_failure.py -q. Then the adjacent suites: tests/test_resume_command.py tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py tests/test_workflow_lisp_procedure_first_migrations.py tests/test_workflow_lisp_lexical_checkpoint_default_resume.py tests/test_runtime_observability.py tests/test_observability_report.py tests/test_monitor_classifier.py tests/test_at68_resume_force_restart.py tests/test_retry_behavior.py. Run pytest --collect-only on every new or renamed test module. As the runtime end-to-end check, run an orchestrator smoke from the repo root: run a small call-using example (e.g. a workflows/examples call demo), interrupt or seed a failed state, run `python -m orchestrator resume <run_id>` cleanly, then corrupt one steps.<name>.step_id and confirm exit 1, the stderr reason and the three-field state delta. Recompile one .orc example to confirm frontend_kind. Check module sizes (wc -l: each new module under 500), confirm state schema 2.1 is unchanged, and grep the auditor for forbidden identifiers. Finally run the full suite (pytest -q) and report any failures with their output; commit incrementally per step with the required Co-Authored-By trailer. Files: none beyond those above (verification only).

findings: Step 1 skips the repository's current prerequisite: docs/design/README.md and docs/plans/2026-07-13-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-design-plan.md say audit placement, failure delta, and schema are unresolved until an accepted target design and independent review. docs/design/resume_projection_integrity_hardening.md does not exist. This plan writes those decisions straight into specs and implementation and leaves docs/index.md, docs/design/README.md, and docs/capability_status_matrix.md still routing readers to design-only work. Complete or explicitly supersede that gate and update the live routing before implementation.

Steps 8-9 violate the stated before-any-mutation/effect boundary. The CLI calls _load_resume_workflow_bundle before its checksum precheck; for .orc, build_frontend_bundle creates .orchestrate/build files before audit. At a reached call, WorkflowExecutor already increments step_visits, may write a debug backup, and calls StateManager.start_step before CallExecutor.execute_call; the plan then audits after visit/start publication and input validation. A nested rejection therefore changes more than root status/error/updated_at. Move the relevant guards earlier or narrow the promised mutation envelope explicitly, with tree snapshots for .orc and nested failures.

Step 8's direct-executor checksum recheck validates the bundle provenance workflow_path against the persisted checksum but never verifies that path is the persisted state.workflow_file. A different bundle with the same source checksum could pass and supply a different projection or source-relative imports. Bind the bundle to the recorded root workflow identity before auditing or executing; test a direct executor given a same-content bundle from another path.

Steps 4 and 6 do not cover a real persisted for_each identity surface. orchestrator/workflow/loops.py persist_for_each_progress stores steps.<loop> as a list of per-iteration result mappings, each able to carry a nested step_id, in addition to flattened steps.<loop>[i].<step> rows. The proposed 'each steps.<name> row' audit either treats that valid list as malformed or skips its explicit IDs. Enumerate and compare both representations, including disagreement between them, before accepting the scope.

Step 6 checks current_step.step_id and presentation ownership but omits current_step.index. StateManager.start_step persists index, and ResumePlanner._projected_current_step already rejects an index that disagrees with the projection. A checksum-compatible corrupt index would pass the new audit and fail later under a different error after prologue mutation. Audit name and index together with step_id, and reject non-mapping current_step through the same stable diagnostic.

The promised stable unsupported_shape/invalid_loop_progress failure cannot be reached for some malformed persisted states at the CLI: StateManager.load calls RunState.from_dict before audit, and from_dict constructs every for_each entry with ForEachState(**state_dict). A non-mapping entry or unexpected key raises before the proposed handler can write resume_projection_integrity_error. Preserve a raw-state read for preflight or normalize these load failures into the same audited envelope; test the public CLI with malformed for_each JSON.

Step 5 groups retry frames by call boundary and calls different base IDs ambiguous, but frame_id_with_overrides makes a new base '<step_id>::visit::<count>' for each legitimate revisit. A call reached twice through routing can retain completed frames for visits 1 and 2, so a later resume would be rejected even though the plan claims any number of completed frames are allowed. Partition lineage by visit family, validate all members, and choose only the reached family's resumable member; include a multi-visit integration test.

Step 10's instruction to stop repeat_until on projection failure is insufficient at the actual propagation point: orchestrator/workflow/loops.py execute_repeat_until wraps a failed nested result in repeat_until_body_step_failed before returning it. The root error would no longer be the required unchanged resume_projection_integrity_error even if routing stops. Bypass that wrapper for this error and test exact root, step, and finalization error identity after a nested repeat_until call fails.

Step 6's diagnostic contract allows any scalar offending_value, scope_path element, and workflow_file without a length or character bound. An attacker-controlled step_id, frame ID, or alias can therefore put a long or private scalar into state.json and stderr while the proposed privacy tests cover only list/mapping IDs and bound inputs. Define bounded, escaped/redacted values for every diagnostic field and test long secret-bearing scalar identities.

Step 1 says to append acceptance entries after item 199, but specs/acceptance/index.md already contains item 200 (Atomic upgrader ownership). Appending 200 again creates duplicate normative IDs; append after 200 and retain its cross-source checksum boundary.

Step 12's full-suite command 'pytest -q' conflicts with this repository's AGENTS.md, which requires broad/slow/full suites to run as 'pytest -q -n 16 --dist=worksteal' and long runs in tmux. Update the verification command and run location before treating the plan's closeout as compliant.

6. Retry lineage indexing (pure, no I/O), partitioned by visit family. New module orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_lineage.py with RetryFrameMember(frame_id, ordinal), CompletedFrameMember(frame_id), CallFrameRetryLineage(base_frame_id, completed_members, failed_predecessors sorted by ordinal, running_member), CallFrameRetryLineageError(ValueError) with .reason, index_retry_lineage(boundary_step_id, frame_items, *, frontend_kind) and next_unused_retry_frame_id(lineage). Frame ids parse strictly. A family base B is the id with no retry marker: the ordinary `[<parent frame id>.]<step_id>::visit::<n>` produced by frame_id_with_overrides. B is ordinal 0, and `B::retry::<n>` needs a positive decimal n without leading zeros, otherwise unsupported_shape; a nested marker is also unsupported_shape. Every frame (completed ones included) is validated for shape, caller (missing_call_boundary when call_step_id is not the boundary), alias (persisted_import_alias_mismatch when aliases differ) and status (unknown -> unsupported_shape). Completed frames are unlimited historical records in any visit family: they never take part in mixed-base, ordinal-gap or running-count checks, so completed frames for visits 1 and 2 of a call reached twice through routing are accepted. Only non-completed members form the lineage. They must all share one family base (otherwise ambiguous_resumable_call_frame: this is the task's 'mixed bases'), have unique ordinals (duplicate -> ambiguous_resumable_call_frame) contiguous from the family's lowest member (gap -> unsupported_shape) and at most one running member (more -> ambiguous_resumable_call_frame). base_frame_id is that family base, or the reached call's ordinary frame id when there are no non-completed members; completed_members lists all completed frames of the boundary. A non-Workflow-Lisp boundary allows at most one non-completed frame (more -> ambiguous_resumable_call_frame), which becomes running_member. next_unused_retry_frame_id returns B::retry::<lowest unused positive ordinal> over all members of family B, including completed frames whose id parses into family B; it ignores completed frames of other visit families and is idempotent.
